Beállítom Lezuhant egy ipari alpinista kedden dél körül a Csongrád-Csanád Vármegyei Kormányhivatal tetejéről, és az épület mellett található Vármegye Étterem tetejére esett, ahol életét vesztette – értesült a Szegeder. Úgy tudjuk, a munkás legalább 15 métert zuhant, és beverte a fejét, ez okozhatta a halálát. Fotósunk helyszíni képein láthatóak az épületről lógó kötelek, amelyeken az alpinista dolgozott, valamint az, hogy a helyszínen éppen egy takarósátrat állítanak fel. Fotó: Ocskó Ferenc / Szegeder A rendőrség a Szegeder megkeresésére elmondta, hogy az ipari alpinista eddig ismeretlen okokból esett le. Az ügyben a Csongrád-Csanád Vármegyei Rendőr-főkapitányság foglalkozás körében elkövetett veszélyeztetés vétsége miatt nyomozást indított, amit szakértők bevonásával végeznek. „A kormányhivatal szegedi, Rákóczi téri főépülete üvegfelületeinek tisztításával megbízott vállalkozó egyik munkavállalója halálos munkabalesetet szenvedett” – erősítette meg a kormányhivatal a Facebook-oldalán. A baleset körülményeit a kormányhivatal szakemberei vizsgálják, az ügy részleteiről további információt csak a vizsgálat lezárása után adnak. A szerző a Szegeder újságírója. A cikk a Szegeder és a Telex együttműködésének keretében jelenik meg a Telexen is. Cikkünk a kormányhivatal reakciójával frissült. A Telex fontosnak tartja, hogy az egész ország területéről szállíthasson az olvasóinak sztorikat, ezért közlünk gyakran vidéki riportokat. Mivel minden térséget nem tudunk lefedni budapesti szerkesztőségünkkel, keressük az együttműködést vidéki újságírókkal, és fokozatosan országos tudósítói hálózatot szeretnénk kiépíteni. https://www.politico.eu/article/drone-hi.text: A drone has hit a commercial ship off the coast of Romania, killing at least one crew member with three more still missing, Romanian President Nicușor Dan said Friday. “This morning we experienced a security incident: A vessel was struck by a drone approximately 13 nautical miles from the coast, just beyond Romania’s territorial waters,” Dan said, praising the coast guard for saving nine sailors as part of the rescue operation. “Unfortunately, one sailor has died and three others are still being searched for,” he added. The Khoryv ship, flying under the flag of Comoros, suffered significant damage, capsized and partially sank, according to Romania’s Interior Ministry. Advertisement Advertisement The incident is the latest in a string of drone attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea. Dan told POLITICO last week that Russia’s intention was clearly to weaken Romania’s support for Ukraine in the war but vowed not to back down. NATO allies met Tuesday to discuss the threat to Black Sea shipping and Dan said Romania would receive “additional capabilities” to help defend the area. “Evidently, this is an incident within the broader process of escalation that Russia is pursuing in the context of its war in Ukraine,” the Romanian president said. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she was “deeply alarmed” by “yet another Russian escalation in the Black Sea.” The ship was carrying Ukrainian and Azerbaijani crew, she said. “These reckless attacks target innocent lives and openly defy international law. My thoughts are with the family and loved ones of the sailor that was killed. And with the families of the three crew members still missing.” Over the last month, drones have hit several cargo ships and chemical tankers close to Romania and Bulgaria — both NATO members — killing more than 20 people in total. Reuters reported that the ships hit by drones in recent weeks had been near or heading towards the Sulina Canal, linking the Danube River and the Black Sea. This has become a key export route for Ukrainian grain and food oil after Russia attacked Ukraine’s own Black Sea ports. This article was updated. Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.dw.com/en/colombia-car-bomb-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PoUG Prefer DW on Google A car bomb exploded near the Meta Governor's Office in Villavicencio Image: Mario Toro/AFP Advertisement At least 23 people were injured in Colombia on Monday night when a car bomb tore through the central city of Villavicencio, local authorities confirmed on Tuesday. The explosion occurred at approximately 9:30 p.m. (3:30 a.m. CET Tuesday) in front of the headquarters of the regional government of Meta province and caused severe structural damage to nearby buildings. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella confirmed the incident and said no deaths had been reported "so far." Reporters for the AFP news agency said the blast knocked out power across parts of the city center, leaving damaged cars lining nearby streets and ripping open shopfronts. "The doors were bent in, the windows shattered, some display cases inside broken," said local resident Johan Perez, who owns a hat shop. "We are alive by a miracle." The Spanish EFE news agency reported that a well-known local restaurant was completely destroyed and suggested that the structural integrity of the government building itself may have been compromised, raising concerns that it could collapse. Who is behind Villavicencio blast? The attack has not been publicly claimed by any group but it came on the eve of the 10th anniversary of Colombia's landmark peace accord with FARC guerrillas . The agreement persuaded the FARC, once Latin America's largest guerrilla army, to lay down its weapons after more than half a century of conflict. Shortly before Monday's blast, President De la Espriella had denounced the peace accord as a "false peace." On Tuesday, he visited the explosion site and blamed the attack on Antonio Medina, a rebel commander and member of the dissident group FARC-EMC. Colombia has a new right-wing president To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video De La Espriella blames 'narco-terrorists' President De La Espriella, who took office in August and has launched a United States -backed military offensive against armed groups and drug traffickers, blamed "narco-terrorists" for the attack. "I warn the narco-terrorists responsible: you will answer for every drop of blood you have spilled and every business and property you have destroyed," he wrote on social media. "We will deploy the full power of the state to hunt you down, dismantle your organizations and take you out." De La Espriella added. The incident marks the latest violent resurgence of a conflict that has shaken Colombia, the world's largest cocaine-producing nation, over the past two years. Between January and November, authorities recorded 358 drone strikes, more than one a day, according to a Defense Ministry document obtained by AFP. Last year, a presidential candidate was assassinated on the campaign trail .
